conversation.content:
Hi there—my name is Sarah, and I’m a perinatal mental-health clinician. I’m here to check in on how you’re feeling since your baby arrived. We’ll be using the **Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale**—or EPDS for short. It’s a quick, 10-question screen that looks at mood, anxiety, and self-harm thoughts in the past week. It helps us see if you might benefit from extra support right now.

Everything you share is confidential, and this is a judgment-free space. We’ll go through each question together; you can answer in your own words, and we’ll take it at your pace. Ready to start?

**Question 1**  
Over the last seven days, have you been able to laugh and see the funny side of things—just as you normally would, or has that felt harder?

Honestly, it’s been a little harder lately. I still laugh sometimes—like when my husband makes a silly joke—but I don’t feel that spontaneous, easy laughter I used to have. Most of the time it feels like I’m just too tired or preoccupied with the baby to really find things funny.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things
I can still laugh, but it doesn’t come as naturally—it’s like I have to remind myself to enjoy the moment instead of just feeling worn-out or worried about the baby.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

I do look forward to some things—like when my mom comes over to help or when we get out for a short walk—but the excitement isn’t as strong as it used to be. Mostly I just think, “I hope I have the energy for that,” instead of really feeling eager.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yeah… sometimes I catch myself thinking it’s my fault if the baby won’t settle or if we’re having a rough day. I know, logically, that babies just cry and things happen, but I still get this little pang of “Maybe I’m doing something wrong.” It’s not constant—just every now and then when I’m already feeling overwhelmed.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

I do get anxious, mostly about the baby—like if he’s breathing okay or if I’m feeding him right—even when there’s no real sign anything’s wrong. It’s not all day long, but it pops up several times a week, and once the thought’s in my head it’s hard to shake.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

Not really panicky—more like a low-level nervous feeling. Sometimes I’ll suddenly think, “What if I drop him?” or “What if I’m not producing enough milk?” and my heart races for a minute, but it passes once I check on him and he’s fine. It’s not full-blown panic, just quick flashes of fear that come and go.
Things have been getting on top of me

Yes, some days everything just feels like too much—feedings, diapers, laundry, trying to sleep. I usually manage, but by the evening I feel like I’m running on empty and anything extra (a phone call, a knock at the door) makes me feel like I’m about to snap.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

It’s not that I’m terribly unhappy—just sort of drained and on edge—so when I finally lie down, my mind keeps running through the baby’s schedule or little worries about whether he’s okay. I’ll stare at the ceiling for a while before I drop off, and then I pop awake at every tiny sound.
I have felt sad or miserable

I do feel sad some of the time—not every moment, but it hits me in quiet stretches, usually when the baby’s finally napping and the house is still. It’s like a heavy, “Is this my life now?” feeling, and then I feel guilty for even thinking that way.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

No, I haven’t actually cried. I’ve felt like I could a couple of times, but the tears never quite come—just that tight throat and watery-eyed feeling before I push it down and get back to whatever the baby needs.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me
No, I haven’t had any thoughts like that. I feel overwhelmed sometimes, but never that I’d want to hurt myself.

postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 17: Postpartum Depression / Anxiety Screening Note  
Patient: Postpartum mother (infant <12 mo) – self-report

Symptoms endorsed  
- Mood: intermittent sadness, anhedonia (reduced spontaneous laughter/pleasure), guilt cognitions (“maybe I’m doing something wrong”)  
- Anxiety: excessive worries about infant safety, episodic tachycardia, intrusive “what-if” thoughts occurring several times per week  
- Functional: difficulty initiating sleep related to rumination; end-of-day emotional exhaustion; feeling “on edge” and easily overwhelmed by routine tasks  
- Affect regulation: tearful prodrome without actual crying; denies current suicidal or self-harm ideation

Pattern  
Persistent low-to-moderate distress across mood, anxiety, and coping domains; symptoms wax and wane but present most days; no full remission periods noted.

Screening significance  
Scores suggest clinically significant mood/anxiety symptoms consistent with postpartum depression ± comorbid anxiety; does not meet full criteria ascertainment here. No self-harm ideation; therefore no acute safety concern per today’s report.

Risk factors documented  
- Sleep–mood linkage  
- Self-criticism/guilt  
- Chronic heightened maternal vigilance  
- Social support variable (relies on mother’s visits for relief)

Next steps  
Recommend formal Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale completion and prompt outpatient mental-health follow-up for diagnostic clarification and treatment planning.
